$comment: D-CSUBSET-INTRINSIC-BSWAP: runtime witness for the 6 byte-swap builtins -- the MSVC `_byteswap_{ushort,ulong,uint64}` family (sqlite's pe path) and the GCC `__builtin_bswap{16,32,64}` family -- all over ONE pure-unary MirOpcode::Bswap, lowered native-or-EXPANDED by a PER-WIDTH capability probe. This single file witnesses BOTH arms of that split at runtime: on x86-64 (pe64 + elf) the u32/u64 cases hit native BSWAP (0F C8+rd) while the two u16 cases take the universal-ALU byte-reversal EXPANSION (x86 has no width-16 BSWAP -- architecturally undefined, GAS refuses `bswap %ax`); on arm64 (elf-aarch64 under qemu + macho-darwin) all three widths are native REV16/REV/REV(X), so the arm64 arms are the only runtime closure for REV16. ★ ANTI-FOLD IS THE CRITICAL PROPERTY HERE and it is the INVERSE of the sync_synchronize_fence example's: Bswap is PURE, so its risk is being FOLDED AWAY (not dropped) -- which would leave the lowering unexercised while the exit code stayed 42. Defences: every operand is read from a MUTABLE STATIC GLOBAL assigned at runtime, and every builtin sits behind a wrapper fn taking the value as an ARG so it survives the `release` arm's Inlining. ✔ VERIFIED that this suffices: MirOpcode::Bswap is NOT in ConstFold's fold set -- src/opt/passes/const_fold.cpp maps only Add/Sub/Mul/SDiv/SMod/And/Or/Xor/Shl/AShr/ICmp*/Neg/Not (+ UDiv/UMod/LShr/ICmpU*) to a HirOpKind, and an unmapped opcode is never folded. ★ CASE 1 CARRIES DELIBERATELY DIRTY UPPER BITS: `(u16)gDirty` with gDirty = 0xDEAD1234 leaves 0xDEAD1234 live in the input register while the VALUE is 0x1234, so the expansion MUST mask each byte before placing it -- the two-instruction `(x<<8)|(x>>8)` form plus a trailing `& 0xFFFF` yields 0x9912 and drops the exit to 41. Values are width-discriminating (both u64 inputs have significant bytes ONLY above bit 32, so a 32-bit miscompile returns 0 in the low half); the six checks carry distinct positive weights 1+2+4+8+16+11 = 42, so the exit code names which one failed and 42 is reachable only when all six hold.
